title: Klee’s measure running-time exponent
formal: For each fixed integer \(d\ge3\), determine to absolute error at most \(1/100\) the optimal deterministic running-time exponent \[x_{\mathrm{Klee}}(d)=\inf\{a\ge0:\text{some uniform exact algorithm has worst-case time }O_d(n^a)\}.\] The task is to compute the exact \(d\)-dimensional volume of the union of \(n\) explicitly given axis-aligned boxes in the real-RAM model below. Programs and constants may depend on fixed \(d\), but not on the coordinates or input size. Logarithmic factors in running time are not part of the numerical answer.
why: A basic measure-computation problem underlying geometric union and coverage algorithms.

progress.text: An exact \(O(n^{d/2})\) static algorithm is obtained for fixed \(d\ge 3\); separate word-RAM improvements use integer-coordinate assumptions.
Faster box-union approximation and a general object-query lower bound are published.
Exact dynamic data structures achieve near-optimal amortized update bounds under a stated combinatorial clique hypothesis, leaving the present unconditional static classification separate.

references.title: Wikipedia: Klee's measure problem
references.locator: Discovery source; retrieved 2026-09-11. Evidence locator: d ≥ 3

definitions: An input is a list of \(n\ge 0\) closed boxes \(B_i=\prod_{j=1}^d[a_{ij},b_{ij}]\), specified by their 2dn finite real endpoints, with \(a_{ij}\le b_{ij}\). Overlaps, coincident endpoints, duplicate boxes and zero side lengths are allowed. The output is the exact Lebesgue measure of \(\bigcup_i B_i\), returned as a real number; the empty union has volume zero. For clarity, the real-RAM convention here is deterministic computation with exact real registers, unit-cost copying, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by nonzero values, comparisons and branching. Random access is through integer addresses. Control and address registers have \(O(\log (n+2))\) bits, with any fixed constant factor depending on the algorithm and d; standard arithmetic, comparison, Boolean and shift operations on these words cost one unit. Integers can be converted to real registers, but real values can affect integer control only through comparisons: no floor, bit extraction or arbitrary real-to-integer conversion is available. A program is finite and independent of n and the coordinates; any hard-coded real constants must be algebraic and finitely specified. Input reads, output writes, preprocessing, memory operations and control steps count. Worst-case time is the maximum over all endpoint lists of size n, regardless of coordinate magnitude. No randomness, approximation tolerance, oracle or precomputed advice depending on n is supplied. For a correct uniform deterministic program \(A\) in fixed dimension \(d\), let \(t_{A,d}(n)\) be its worst-case time on \(n\) boxes. Define \[x_{\mathrm{Klee}}(d)=\inf\{a\ge0:\exists A\ \exists C>0\ \exists n_0\ge1\ \forall n\ge n_0,\ t_{A,d}(n)\le Cn^a\}.\] A different uniform program may be selected for each fixed dimension and each exponent bound, but not for each input length. Elementary input access and the cited algorithm give \(1\le x_{\mathrm{Klee}}(d)\le d/2\). The infimum need not be attained; in particular a value does not prescribe matching logarithmic factors. A lower bound must concern every permitted exact program, without an unproved complexity assumption.
answer_criterion: Supply an unambiguously specified real answer \(a(d)\) for every integer \(d\ge3\) and a complete Lean-checked proof of absolute error at most \(1/100\) in the defined exponent. A certified enclosing interval of width at most \(1/50\) qualifies via its midpoint. Both sides of the interval must be justified. An exact value also qualifies. The infimum need not be attained, and no ordinary logarithmic growth limit is assumed. Matching logarithmic factors, leading constants and an algorithm attaining the endpoint exponent are not required. A one-sided improvement alone qualifies only if the resulting certified interval is sufficiently narrow.

context_blocks.title: Overlap counts only once
context_blocks.text: Two boxes may cover the same region, so adding their individual volumes overcounts their intersection. In three dimensions, \([0,2]^{3}\) and \([1,3]\times [0,2]^{2}\) each have volume 8, but their union has volume 12. The task requests this single total volume; it does not request a full description of the union boundary. In higher dimensions a box is simply a product of intervals.

context_blocks.title: The known exact bound
context_blocks.text: Chan’s 2013 algorithm computes exact union volume in \(O(n^{d/2})\) time for every fixed \(d\ge3\). This gives the finite upper bound \(x_{\mathrm{Klee}}(d)\le d/2\). Connections with clique problems provide conditional evidence, not an unconditional lower bound for all algorithms.

context_blocks.title: Why numerical conventions matter
context_blocks.text: The real-RAM question counts an arithmetic operation on a coordinate as one step even when the coordinate would require many bits to encode. Chan also obtains logarithmic improvements for integer coordinates in a word-RAM setting. Those improvements do not automatically transfer to unrestricted real inputs, and the source explicitly discusses this distinction. The detailed primitive and worst-case conventions above make the inherited real-RAM target explicit.

context_blocks.title: Recent advances concern other guarantees
context_blocks.text: The SoCG 2025 work speeds up approximation of union volume and proves a lower bound for algorithms restricted to certain object queries. A small relative error is permitted there. The ICALP 2026 work maintains exact volume under insertions and deletions and measures amortized update time. Both are significant results, but neither determines the unconditional optimal time of a single exact static computation in this card’s model.

sentences: Klee’s measure problem computes the volume covered by a union of axis-aligned boxes.
Overlaps count once, and the requested volume is exact.
The card asks for the optimal deterministic running-time exponent in every fixed dimension at least three.
Each exponent must be certified to absolute error 0.01.
Logarithmic factors and a fastest algorithm attaining the infimum are not required.
